name: Texel.ai

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Not a compute product. Texel sells per-job media-AI API calls (lip sync, NVIDIA Maxine eye-contact, studio voice, video encode, image/video generation). The live billing API itemises each job as billable_seconds x rate_per_minute with a per-job minimum_seconds; only successful jobs are charged. No numeric rate_per_minute or minimum_seconds is published (texel.ai/pricing is 404). Rates stay null; never interpret as free.

caveats: Current public API focuses on AI media creation/editing. YC describes GPU pipeline deployment. No current arbitrary-code CPU/GPU rate verified, so keep marginal rather than assert a general sandbox product.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

No public price list as of 2026-09-29: texel.ai/pricing returns 404 and the homepage says only 'Straightforward pricing / Pay only for what you use'. Billing is per-job, per media minute (rate_per_minute, minimum_seconds) via GET /v1/billing/usage. A credit-based pricing page (100 credits/prompt image gen, 1000 credits/model training, 5,000 free credits on sign-up, Enterprise by contact) existed Dec 2023 to at least Sep 2024 (Wayback) but is withdrawn and the credit-to-USD rate was never published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: Not applicable: Texel.ai sells a hosted media-AI job API (lipsync, Stable Diffusion txt2img/img2img/txt2vid/img2vid, video encoding, billing usage). The complete public OpenAPI has no machine, sandbox or instance resource, so there is nothing to snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint among the 14 public endpoints; no user-visible machines.

harness_api.note: Job-based media API only; no agent harness or code execution.

egress_allowlist.note: No user code runs on Texel, so no egress controls exist/apply.

ingress_rules.note: Not applicable: no exposed ports; only the bearer-token-authenticated Texel API.

guest_firewall.note: No guest OS access at all.

secret_proxy.note: No proxy. Output-to-your-bucket options take S3-style bucket/access_key/secret_key fields directly in the job request body.

volume_attach.note: No volumes; inputs/outputs are URLs or customer buckets.

max_session_h.quote: billable_seconds x rate_per_minute with a per-job minimum_seconds
max_session_h.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Texel has no persistent session/machine at all — it's a stateless per-job API (submit a media job, get billed per job, poll/webhook for result), so there is no session duration limit to hit; 'none' reflects there being no session construct rather than an unlimited long-running machine.

usage_api.quote: Texel.ai is not a sandbox/VM provider; it is a hosted job-based media-AI API service (lipsync, image/video generation, encoding). usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; The product's scope is discrete media generation jobs, not persistent compute resources. The billing API itemizes each job by billable_seconds and rate_per_minute, but this does not address the use case of tracking separate sandbox/VM usage to bill customers with their own machines.
